Qwen3.8-27B just got another acceleration path on Apple Silicon.

Rapid-MLX v0.15.4 adds a dedicated TensorFold profile paired with a DFlash2 speculative drafter, with a reported 1.72x speedup.

The interesting part is that the model itself didn’t change.

The inference stack did.

DFlash2 works by having a smaller drafter propose multiple future tokens before the 27B target model verifies them. When enough predictions are accepted, the target model can produce more tokens per expensive forward pass.

That can turn a sequential decoding bottleneck into something much more parallel.

And this isn’t limited to Qwen3.8-27B.

GLM-5.3 Flash now gets MTP-head acceleration out of the box, with reported generation speeds approaching 2x.

MTP gives the target model another mechanism for predicting future tokens, which can then be verified together rather than generated strictly one at a time.

Rapid-MLX is also attacking a completely different bottleneck: concurrency.

The new opt-in lane matmul path targets workloads with 8+ concurrent requests, where the inference problem changes significantly compared with a single-user session.

The reported decode gains are 50–81%.

So this release has three pretty different optimization paths:

Qwen3.8-27B
TensorFold + DFlash2
~1.72x reported speedup

GLM-5.3 Flash
MTP acceleration
Nearly 2x reported generation

8+ concurrent requests
Lane matmul
50–81% reported decode gains

And this is exactly why Apple Silicon local inference has become so interesting.

The hardware hasn’t changed.

The model hasn’t changed.

The runtime keeps getting smarter about how it uses both.

We’ve seen the same Qwen3.8-27B model produce very different numbers depending on the inference engine, speculative decoder, quantization, memory layout and workload.

TensorFold is pushing that optimization layer further, and Rapid-MLX is bringing those ideas into the MLX ecosystem.

The bigger lesson is that local AI performance is becoming less about asking:

“How fast is this model?”

And more about asking:

“How efficiently can this inference stack make the model use the hardware?”

Because there is still a lot of performance hiding inside the software.

Rapid-MLX v0.15.4 is another example of finding it.

【サイバーセキュリティ動向分析】

2026年10月3日時点のサイバーセキュリティ動向は、AI関連コンポーネントの重大脆弱性、既知のゼロデイ悪用、パッチ適用後の運用障害、国家関連のスパイ活動、そして日本国内の制度変更が重なる局面にある。以下、直近で注目すべきトピックごとに背景・影響・対策を整理する。
GitLabの自己ホスト型AI Gatewayに、認証済み利用者による任意コマンド実行を許す重大な欠陥が確認された。識別子はCVE-2026-90970で、深刻度は9.9とされる。AI GatewayはGitLabインスタンスと外部のAIモデルをつなぐ中継サービスであり、Duo Agent Platformを利用する環境で条件が揃うと、ログイン済みの攻撃者がゲートウェイ上でコマンドを走らせられる。自己ホストでゲートウェイを運用している組織に限定されるが、ソースコードやCI/CDの機密が集まる場所だけに、侵害時の波及は開発パイプライン全体に及ぶ。GitLabは10月2日に修正版（19.2.4、19.3.2、19.4.1）を公開し、該当顧客へ即時更新を強く求めている。対策は修正版への速やかな更新、ゲートウェイへのアクセスを必要最小限のアカウントに絞ること、コマンド実行や異常なプロセス生成の監視を強化することである。クラウド版を利用している場合は影響範囲外だが、自己ホスト構成の有無を棚卸ししておく必要がある。
DellのContainer Storage Modules（CSM）では、認証を欠く重大な欠陥が複数公表された。なかでもCVE-2026-63688は深刻度10.0で、csm-authorization-storageのgRPCサーバに対し、未認証の遠隔攻撃者が登録済みストレージアレイの管理者資格情報を取得できる。Kubernetesノード上でのroot権限取得につながる経路も指摘されている。エンタープライズストレージとコンテナ基盤を結ぶコンポーネントだけに、侵害されるとデータボリュームの改ざんや横展開の足がかりになりやすい。Dellはセキュリティ更新DSA-2026-448を出し、管理者に早期適用を求めている。対策はベンダー提供の修正適用、ストレージ管理インターフェースのネットワーク分離、gRPCエンドポイントの露出確認、資格情報のローテーション、Kubernetes側の権限最小化である。
Fortinet FortiMailのゼロデイCVE-2026-104286が実環境で悪用されている。パス走査とNULLバイト処理の不備により、未認証の攻撃者が細工したHTTP/HTTPSリクエストで基盤システムへ任意ファイルを書き込める。深刻度は9.8前後とされ、米国CISAの既知悪用脆弱性カタログに追加された。メールゲートウェイは外部に晒されやすく、書き込み成功後は不正コードの配置や設定改ざんへ発展しうる。一部ブランチでは修正が未提供の時点で、FortinetはIBE機能の無効化と管理インターフェースのインターネット遮断を暫定措置として推奨し、攻撃元IPやファイルベースの痕跡も公開している。米連邦民間機関には10月4日までの対応期限が示された。対策は暫定措置の即時実施、修正公開後の適用、管理画面のアクセス制限、メールゲートウェイのログと書き込み痕跡の点検である。
ヘルプデスク製品Zammadのゼロデイ2件（CVE-2026-102489とCVE-2026-102490）が、オランダの脆弱性開示機関DIVDへの侵入で連鎖的に使われた。セッション固定によりzammadユーザーとして遠隔コード実行が可能になり、ローカル権限の不備と組み合わせてrootまで昇格できる。報告では、数秒規模で権限昇格まで進み、他サービスへの移動とデータ持ち出しが行われ、ボランティアのメールアドレスなどが影響を受けた可能性がある。攻撃はエージェント型AIを活用したものと説明されており、自動化された探索と悪用の速度が従来の人手攻撃を上回る事例として注目されている。CISAも既知悪用リストに加え、短期の修正期限を設けた。対策はベンダー修正の適用、セッション管理の強化、ヘルプデスクをインターネットから切り離すか多要素認証とIP制限を掛けること、zammadユーザーの権限監査、異常なセッション固定や権限昇格の検知である。
Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gatewayでは、未認証の遠隔コード実行を許すゼロデイ（CVE-2026-88771、CVE-2026-88772など）が実悪用された後、緊急パッチが公開された。しかしビルド14.1-73.37適用後に、特にSAML認証を使う環境でアプライアンスが繰り返し再起動する不具合が報告されている。リモートアクセスの要となる機器だけに、パッチ前は侵害リスク、パッチ後は可用性低下という二重の負担が生じている。政府・金融などへの攻撃が確認されたとの情報もある。対策はベンダーが示す安定版または回避手順の確認、SAML設定の切り分け、管理インターフェースの露出最小化、セッションと設定変更の監査、代替リモートアクセス経路の準備である。
中国関連とみられる脅威クラスタによるスパイ活動も続いている。Cisco Talosなどが追跡する活動では、Antinoと呼ばれるバックドアがOutlookやOneDriveをコマンド＆コントロールに使い、正規のMicrosoft 365通信に紛れてアジア各地の政府・政策機関を狙っている。対象には台湾、インド、フィリピン、カンボジア、パキスタン、タイ、ミャンマーなどが挙げられている。クラウドの正規サービスを隠れ蓑にするため、従来の境界型検知では見逃しやすい。影響は政策文書や連絡先の長期的な窃取、その後のなりすましである。対策はMicrosoft 365の異常なOAuth同意や外部共有の監査、条件付きアクセスの強化、エンドポイントでの不審なプロセスとクラウドAPI呼び出しの相関分析、標的型フィッシング対策の継続である。
IoT分野では、Clingと呼ばれるボットネットが確認された。コマンド＆コントロール通信をGoogleの公開STUNトラフィックに偽装し、Realtek Jungle SDK（2.0から3.4.14B）の未認証遠隔コマンド実行欠陥を悪用する。UDPパケットの先頭に特定文字列を付けてシェルコマンドを送る手法で、露出した機器を掌握する。家庭・業務用の組み込み機器が踏み台やDDoS源になるリスクがある。対策は該当SDKを使う機器のファームウェア更新、管理ポートのインターネット露出禁止、異常なSTUN様UDPの監視、不要なUPnPやリモート管理の無効化である。
Microsoftが公開した年次脅威報告（Digital Defense Report 2026）では、観測した侵入の約63％でデータ窃取が伴い、外部から到達可能なクラウド環境は平均5.3時間で攻撃を受けていたとされた。ランサムウェアの実行件数は前年比で増加し、重要製造業が標的の上位に入る。企業の多くがAIエージェントを試験導入または拡大予定であり、2028年には稼働エージェントが膨大な数に達するとの予測も示された。エージェントは新たな攻撃面になり、資格情報の悪用、過剰な権限、プロンプト経由の不正操作が懸念される。対策はエージェントの最小権限化、高影響操作の人間承認、クラウドの露出資産の継続棚卸し、アイデンティティ基盤の多要素認証と条件付きアクセス、データ窃取の出口監視である。
日本国内では、10月1日にサイバー対処能力強化法（能動的サイバー防御関連法）が施行された。15分野・約258の基幹インフラ事業者を対象に、攻撃の兆候を検知した場合の政府への報告義務が課される。警察と自衛隊は、一定の要件のもとで攻撃元サーバへの侵入による無害化措置を実施できる体制を強化する。背景には、重要インフラへの先制的・破壊的攻撃への対応力不足がある。事業者側は報告フロー、検知基準、取引先や委託先を含むサプライチェーンの情報共有を整備する必要がある。対策は対象該当性の確認、インシデント報告手順の明文化、ログ保全と政府連携窓口の整備、無害化措置が自社資産に及ぶ場合の影響評価である。
その他、cPanel/WHMでは管理者セッションの乗っ取りやrootでの任意コマンド実行を許す欠陥（CVE-2026-93698など）が修正された。全サポート版が影響し、ホスティング事業者は優先更新が必要だ。SharePointの既知脆弱性を悪用する中国系ランサムウェア集団Warlockは、水道、通信、地方行政、大学などを標的にしている。教育関連ではFrontline Educationが第三者ソフトの欠陥経由で従業員情報（社会保障番号を含む）の窃取を通知した。WordPressプラグインでも認証回避や権限昇格が複数報告されている。暗号資産取引所Bitgetでは、外部セキュリティサービスのゼロデイ経由で約3億8750万ドル規模の窃取が確認された。Microsoft公式のXアカウントが一時的に乗っ取られ、暗号トークンの宣伝に使われた事案もある。
全体として、AIコンポーネントと境界機器のゼロデイが同時に悪用され、パッチ自体が可用性を損なうケースも出ている。優先すべきは、インターネット露出の高いメール・リモートアクセス・ストレージ管理・AIゲートウェイの棚卸しと、既知悪用リストに載った欠陥の暫定措置または修正適用である。あわせて、エージェントとクラウド資格情報の権限を絞り、正規クラウドサービスを悪用する通信の異常を検知できるよう監視を広げることが、当面の実効的な防御になる。

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next can now fit on a single 32GB GPU, and the reported speed is already above 80 tok/s.

This is a preview release from AgentionAI, built specifically around making the huge Flash Next architecture practical on smaller GPUs.

The hardware target:

32GB VRAM

And the reported result:

80+ tok/s on a single Radeon R9700 PRO

That’s pretty wild considering what is actually being squeezed onto that card.

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next is a massive MoE architecture with a very large parameter count, so simply taking the standard Q4 model and trying to squeeze it into 32GB isn’t the answer.

The trick is in the quantization and inference stack.

This preview uses a specialized low-bit format designed to reduce the memory footprint enough for the model to become viable on a 32GB card, while keeping the model usable rather than turning it into a tiny, heavily compromised approximation.

And that distinction matters.

“Fits in 32GB” is one benchmark.

“Fits in 32GB and actually runs fast enough to use” is another.

The reported 80+ tok/s makes this much more interesting.

For comparison, the standard Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model is designed around a much larger memory footprint, and the official architecture includes a huge n-gram embedding component alongside its MoE layers. (huggingface. co)

Community inference work has already shown how much the right quantization strategy can change the hardware requirements.

AgentionAI’s newer 32GB-focused Gyro quant, for example, reports around 28.8 GiB of GPU memory at 64K context, with the large n-gram table kept off the GPU. It uses rotor-based quantization for the routed experts rather than applying one conventional quantization type everywhere. (huggingface. co)

That’s the direction local inference is heading.

Instead of asking:

“How much VRAM does the original model need?”

We’re increasingly asking:

“How much of this model can we compress, offload and restructure without destroying the useful behavior?”

And Qwen3.8-Flash-Next is a perfect example.

The model is huge.

But the active computation per token is much smaller because of its MoE architecture, while its n-gram embedding system provides another way to scale parameters without making every parameter expensive to compute. Qwen describes the architecture as combining hybrid attention with QSA, gated residuals and n-gram embeddings specifically to improve efficiency at scale. (huggingface. co)

The current release is still a preview, though.

That means I wouldn’t treat 80+ tok/s as a universal expectation for every 32GB card.

The whole point of this release is to get more people testing it.

Different AMD cards.

Different NVIDIA cards.

Different drivers.

Different context lengths.

Different inference backends.

Different speculative decoding setups.

And those details can change the result dramatically.

The roadmap is already interesting:

32GB: available now

48GB: coming

64GB: coming

Further performance optimizations: coming

That’s the part I’m watching.

Because once you have a usable 32GB version doing 80+ tok/s, the next question isn’t whether the model can run locally.

It’s how much performance the same approach can unlock when you give it 48GB or 64GB of VRAM.

We’re getting closer to a world where enormous models aren’t automatically reserved for datacenter hardware.

The quantization strategy is becoming part of the model’s deployment architecture.

And Qwen3.8-Flash-Next is turning into a very good example of that.

Meet Noah Shinn: The 23-year-old college dropout whose viral AI assistant is emerging as a new challenger to Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta | Marco Quiroz-Gutierrez, Fortune

At just 23 years old, Noah Shinn is already making his mark on the AI world.

He founded Instinct, an AI assistant startup, just last year. Since then, its valuation has skyrocketed. The company raised $250 million at a $2.5 billion valuation in August, bringing its total raised at the time to $350 million. Just this week, the company raised an additional $1 billion in a Series C that shot its valuation up to $10 billion.

Even though Instinct’s AI assistant is open only to a select few invitees, Instinct is now approaching $1 billion in annual transaction volume, Shinn said in an interview on the Invest Like the Best podcast published Monday.

Despite not being broadly available, Instinct has grown organically through word of mouth, Shinn told the podcast host and venture capitalist Patrick O’Shaughnessy. So many people want to join, he said, that existing users are now selling invitations to join Instinct on eBay.

“We spent $0 on marketing so far,” he said.

What does Instinct do?

Instinct is a free personal assistant powered by AI that can communicate with users via message or a phone call. The assistant launched in private beta in February, The Wall Street Journal reported, but last month opened in an invite-only beta, with each user allotted five invites. It has caught on with people who have used the tool to plan weddings and cancel hundreds of dollars worth of subscriptions, Shinn said in an X post last month.

The Instinct founder said his personal assistant and others like it have the potential to simplify users’ lives, especially when it comes to travel—a category which makes up half of the billion dollars Shinn said is transacting through the platform on a yearly basis—by learning users’ preferences and storing it in its memory.

“It will be able to use that memory and be able to, you know, now make it a much easier experience for you in the future to be able to book that according to exactly what you want,” he said on the podcast.

Taking on Meta

Instinct may have raised hundreds of millions of dollars in funding, but what may say the most about the excitement surrounding it is that the company has also caught the eye of Meta chief AI officer Alexandr Wang, who has poked fun at the company several times in X posts since Meta announced its own personal AI agent, Muse, earlier this month.

Wang, who became a billionaire after founding Scale AI, which Meta later put $14.3 billion into, replied to several posts comparing Muse and Instinct. In one, he said Muse would beat Instinct in an MMA match, while in another he wrote “Muse is way hotter than the other personal agents (and also way faster, but mostly hotter)” in response to another users’ post that meme’d the choice between Instinct and Muse.

Wang last week replied to one more post by mocking Instinct’s name: “Muse absolutely crushes Insect,” he wrote. Shinn reportedly replied to one of Wang’s multiple posts with a smiley face.

Instinct did not immediately reply to Fortune’s request for comment. Meta did not immediately reply to Fortune’s request for comment.

It’s unclear how many users Instinct has at the moment, but Muse, for its part, has already attracted a huge following of its own and recently replaced ChatGPT as the top free app on the U.S. App Store. Estimates from market intelligence provider Apptopia found that Muse saw 2.8 million installs worldwide in its first 12 days, TechCrunch reported.

Shinn said in the interview with O’Shaughnessy that he believes Muse is a great product but that he spends “very little of my time thinking about competition and other players in the space.”

He said right now the potential for growth is huge because many people, even if they use AI, aren’t using it to its highest potential.

“It’s still an exciting time,” he said.

Wang’s posts, though, may have also given Instinct a marketing boost. Combined, Wang got hundreds of thousands of views and more than 1,000 likes on his posts related to Instinct.

Who is Noah Shinn?

Despite the tension, Shinn and Wang have one thing in common. Like many successful tech founders, they both dropped out of college.

Shinn grew up in the San Francisco Bay Area and went to a private high school in San Jose, Business Insider reported. In high school, he played basketball and also ran cross country. He attended Northeastern University in Boston, but left in 2023 to join the startup world.

But Shinn’s work on AI agents began even before he dropped out.

As a student, Shinn had varied interests. If I had 6 months to become an AI Evals Engineer.

I’d do this.

Stage 1: Testing Foundations and Statistics for AI
- Learn: pytest (fixtures, parametrize), JSONL pipelines, precision/recall/F1, confidence intervals, Cohen's kappa.

- Practice:  Build a pytest plugin that loads a JSONL eval dataset and emits a metric report on every run.

- Why:  Evals are tests and tests are math. If you cannot quantify agreement, you cannot prove improvement.

Stage 2: LLM Failure Modes and Behavior
- Learn:  temperature and top-p sampling, seed control, tokenization edge cases, instruction drift, hallucination taxonomies.

- Practice:  Fuzz one model with 500 adversarial inputs and classify every failure into a taxonomy with reproduction steps.

- Why:  Every eval suite is a map of known failure modes. You cannot evaluate what you do not understand.

Stage 3: Golden Dataset Engineering
- Learn:  annotation guidelines, stratified sampling, inter-annotator agreement, dataset versioning, contamination detection.

- Practice:  Build a 300-case golden dataset with 2 annotators, measure kappa, and version it in git with a changelog.

- Why:  Your evals are only as good as your dataset. Garbage labels produce garbage confidence.

Stage 4: Scoring Methods and LLM-as-a-Judge
- Learn:  exact and fuzzy match, embedding similarity, rubric design, judge model selection, judge biases (verbosity, position, self-preference).

- Practice:  Build an LLM-as-a-judge with a rubric, calibrate it against 100 human labels and publish the agreement score.

- Why:  Judges drift and lie. Calibrated judges are instruments; uncalibrated ones are vibes.

Stage 5: RAG Evaluation
- Learn:  hit rate, MRR, NDCG, recall@k, faithfulness vs relevance, citation grounding, abstention quality.

- Practice:  Build a RAG eval harness with separate retrieval and generation gates, plus adversarial queries that must return "no answer".

- Why:  RAG fails in two places. A single score hides which one is broken.

Stage 6: Agent and Trajectory Evaluation
- Learn:  tool-call correctness, step-level grading, trajectory distance metrics, counterfactual replay, sandboxed execution scoring.

- Practice:  Build a trajectory grader that scores each tool call against a golden path and blocks dangerous action sequences.

- Why:  Final-answer evals hide where agents actually break. The trajectory is the unit of accountability.

Stage 7: Eval Frameworks and Custom Harnesses
- Learn:  DeepEval, promptfoo, RAGAS, Braintrust, OpenAI Evals; dataset-driven pipelines, parameterized configs.

- Practice:  Write a custom harness that runs 3 frameworks behind one CLI and outputs a unified metric report.

- Why:  Frameworks give you scaffolding. A custom harness gives you control when the scaffolding lies.

Stage 8: Statistical Rigor for Eval Deltas
- Learn:  bootstrap confidence intervals, paired significance tests, effect size, sample-size math, seed variance.

- Practice:  Build a comparison report that says "Model B wins by 3.2% ± 1.1% (p<0.05)" instead of "Model B seems better".

- Why:  A 2-point difference on 50 samples is noise. Executives make million-dollar decisions on your numbers.

Stage 9: CI/CD Eval Gates and Regression Control
- Learn:  GitHub Actions eval jobs, thresholds with hysteresis, eval caching, cost budgets, flaky-eval detection.

- Practice:  Wire a gate that blocks merges when task success drops >2% vs main and auto-posts failing cases to the PR.

- Why:  Evals that do not block deploys are reports not gates.

Stage 10: Production Monitoring and Drift Detection
- Learn:  Langfuse, LangSmith, Phoenix, traffic sampling strategies, drift metrics, hallucination spike alerts, feedback-trace correlation.

- Practice:  Build a pipeline that samples 5% of prod traffic nightly, runs offline evals and alerts on quality decay.

- Why:  Golden datasets go stale. Production is the eval suite that never stops updating.

Stage 11: Data Flywheels and Eval-Driven Optimization
- Learn:  feedback-to-dataset loops, DPO preference pairs, eval-driven prompt optimization (DSPy), A/B testing with guardrail metrics.

- Practice:  Automate the loop: thumbs-down → labeled case → golden set addition → nightly eval run → diff report.

- Why:  The compounding advantage in AI is not the model. It is the flywheel that converts failures into tests.

Stage 12: Red-Teaming, Public Benchmarks and Portfolio
- Learn:  adversarial suites (injection, jailbreaks, data exfiltration), benchmark methodology, contamination-aware reporting.

- Practice:  Publish a public eval teardown of your agent vs a naive baseline with full methodology and reproducible seeds.

- Why:  Senior evals engineers are hired for their methodology not their dashboards.

Vibe-checking is dead. If you cannot measure it, you cannot ship it.
The modern AI Evals Engineer builds the quality gates for every autonomous system.

There’s a strange problem with teaching robots.

AI models had the entire internet to learn from.

Robots don’t.

   An LLM can learn what a cup is by seeing millions of examples online.
But knowing what a cup is isn’t the same as knowing how to pick it up without dropping it.

For that, robots need action data.
🔹 How to grasp. 🔹 How to move. 🔹 How much force to use. 🔹 How to react when something goes wrong.

And collecting that kind of data with physical robots is expensive and difficult.
That’s the bottleneck.

So what if collecting robot training data worked more like playing a game?
That’s the interesting idea behind @axisrobotics 

➠● Step 1: Open your browser.
You don’t need a physical robot sitting in your room.

➠● Step 2: Control a virtual robot.
Use teleoperation to guide a simulated robot arm through different tasks.

➠● Step 3: Complete the task.
Your movements create a robot trajectory that can become useful training data.

➠● Step 4: The data gets verified.
Instead of random demonstrations disappearing into a database, AXIS is building a participatory, on-chain system around the data.

 ➠● Step 5: Repeat at global scale.
One person generating one trajectory isn’t the breakthrough.

Thousands of people generating different tasks, movements and corrections is where the compounding starts.

That’s how a data famine can become a data engine.

And the numbers are starting to show what that can look like.

September was a month where @axisrobotics moved from promising numbers to tangible proof.

𝗦𝘁𝗮𝘆 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗺𝗲….

 The data engine crossed 5M robot trajectories on @base and has now grown beyond 6M, with 200K+ contributors worldwide.

But the growth wasn’t limited to data.

Axis’ Franka dataset family crossed 160K+ downloads on @huggingface, becoming the most downloaded open-source collection of simulated Franka manipulation data.

The research side also accelerated.
Their work on Embodied RSI showed how deployed policies can generate data that trains stronger successors, pushing success from 22% to 52%.

They also introduced the Open Axis Benchmark with @openroboto a living benchmark built around 6,000+ tasks and 5.5M+ trajectories, designed to keep evaluation evolving alongside robotic models.

  Then came the community milestone.
The Axis Community Sale on Sonar attracted 2,472 participants who committed 2.39M USDC, making it the most participated Sonar sale of 2026.

Axis followed that with a bonus mechanism:
 25% unlocked at TGE for everyone, plus additional bonus tokens fully unlocked at TGE based on original commitments before pro-rata dilution.

The community engine kept moving too:
• 2,521 contributors in the Axis × @BinanceWallet campaign • 477,461 task completions • 989 tasks covered • Challenger Program launched for top-performing contributors • Kaito Content Creator Program entered Epoch 2
And on the institutional/research side, 

Axis’ CEO Chris sat down with Brian Armstrong to discuss how Physical AI is being built, while Axis’ research was accepted into the Physical World Models workshop at IROS 2026.
 
   September wasn’t just about announcing progress.
It was about showing the data, research, participation and infrastructure behind the vision.

  Physical AI needs more than models.
It needs a continuously growing stream of real-world experience to make those models better.

That’s what Axis is building.

Make contributing to Physical AI accessible to anyone with a browser, while creating the diverse Robot Data that future Embodied AI systems need.

Qwen3.8-27B just hit around 381 tok/s on a single RTX 3090.

24GB of VRAM.

250W.

But there is a very important detail behind that number.

This isn’t normal-chat generation.

The breakthrough came from changing how speculative decoding uses the information already sitting inside the prompt.

The progression is pretty wild:

~82 tok/s
Initial single-user setup

~114 tok/s
Optimized MTP

~138 tok/s
DFlash2 + lookup-augmented drafting

~381 tok/s
Longer verification blocks + context lookup

Same GPU throughout.

1x RTX 3090, 24GB VRAM.

The inference stack is doing most of the heavy lifting.

The setup combines Qwen3.8-27B with heavily optimized vLLM, DFlash2 speculative decoding, lookup-based drafting, prefix caching, quantized KV cache, optimized heads and activations, and split-KV verification attention.

But the clever part is the verification step.

DFlash2 normally proposes around 7 tokens for the target model to verify.

The developer realized something important:

The verification block doesn’t have to stop at the number of tokens the drafter proposes.

If the model is answering from a document that is already inside the context, the system can use that context to fill additional draft positions.

So instead of verifying roughly 7 tokens, the target model can verify 16 tokens in one step.

The extra positions don’t need an expensive new prediction from the drafter because the required tokens are already sitting in the prompt.

And that changes the throughput dramatically.

On a roughly 25K-token document reproduction workload:

DFlash2: ~260 tok/s
Longer verification + context lookup: ~382 tok/s

The reported acceptance rate was around 15 of 16 tokens per verification step.

That’s where the 381 tok/s headline comes from.

The model isn’t suddenly capable of generating arbitrary text at 381 tokens every second.

The system is exploiting a very specific property of the workload:

The answer is already somewhere in the context.

Instead of making the GPU predict every token from scratch, the inference stack finds likely tokens directly from the existing context and lets the target model verify large blocks efficiently.

That makes this particularly interesting for workloads like:

RAG and document Q&A

Large-document extraction

Document reproduction or rewriting

Coding agents applying edits

Quoting existing material

Long-context transformations

And there is another optimization that fits perfectly with these workloads: prefix caching.

Once a 25K-token document has already been processed, the next question doesn’t need to process the entire prefix again.

The reported TTFT for a second question drops from roughly:

22.4 seconds → 0.56 seconds

The cached attention KV and recurrent state can be reused instead of rebuilding the entire context.

That is a massive difference for RAG and coding-agent workflows where the same large context gets queried repeatedly.

There is also an important reality check.

On ordinary chat prompts, the same setup is around 133 tok/s, not 381 tok/s. The 16-token verification mode is specifically useful when the answer is strongly grounded in existing context, and it comes with a memory tradeoff that reduces available request slots and context capacity.

So this isn’t really a story about building a “381 tok/s chatbot.”

It’s a story about designing the inference engine around the workload.

The developer combined:

Speculative decoding
Context lookup
Longer verification blocks
Prefix caching
Quantized KV and activations

And the result is an inference system that can exploit something deceptively simple:

Sometimes the model doesn’t need to predict the answer. It already has the answer in front of it.

The context becomes part of the drafting mechanism.

That’s a fascinating direction for local inference. https://t.co/AlxGxC0hoI

Cloudflare 的 Matt Carey 刚刚公布了 agents SDK v0.26.0 的重磅更新：正式原生支持将 Pi 运行在 Durable Objects（DO）之上。现在只需一条命令 npm i agents 即可上手。

这次更新背后的核心看点与技术演进：

有状态智能体落地边缘（Stateful Agents at the Edge）从公布的代码实现来看，通过 @earendil-works/pi-durable 与 PiHarness 抽象，开发者可以直接把 Pi 的运行时无缝挂载到 Durable Object 的生命周期中。Agent 获得了原生的近场计算、内存持久化与存储（Storage）绑定，无需再在中心化服务器与外部数据库之间来回折腾上下文同步。

Pi Harness 迎来 v1.0 发布由 Mario Zechner（@badlogicgames）等人操刀的 Pi（@pidotdev）正式迈入 v1.0。“There are many agent harnesses, but this one is yours”——相比庞大笨重的大模型编排框架，Pi 保持了极高的可塑性与轻量特性，专注于为开发者提供干净、低侵入的模型调度底座。

基础设施层面的百花齐放Matt Carey 提到该方案不仅适用于 Agents SDK，同样兼容普通 Durable Object；而 Node/Deno 之父 Ryan Dahl 也随即在评论区互动，透露 Deno 团队近期也在轻量隔离沙箱 celld 中测试了 Pi 的运行方案。

架构趋势观察：

AI Agent 的基础设施正在快速从传统的中心化后端向“边缘分布式计算 + 极简 Harness”迁移。无论是 Cloudflare DO 带来的分布式状态协同，还是 Deno celld 的极速隔离环境，都在证明一点：下一代生产级 Agent 拼的不只是 Prompt，更是毫秒级的边缘响应、持久化状态与隔离执行能力。

7 万多 star、GitHub 把主要语言标成 C、README 里又写着内核由 Rust 驱动。这个组合让我先去翻了一遍它到底在做什么。

它要解决的是哪个问题？

编码 agent 理解一个陌生代码库的方式其实很原始：grep 找名字，glob 列文件，Read 一个一个读，然后在上下文里自己把调用链拼回来。真正开始改代码之前，已经烧掉一堆工具调用和往返。CodeGraph 的做法是提前把每个符号、每条调用边、每个依赖建成一张图，agent 问一次，拿回相关源码、符号之间的调用路径，以及这次改动的影响范围。

和自己写个 grep 脚本比，差别在哪？

差在动态分发。接口、回调、运行时派发这类跳转，文本搜索本来就跟不动，而图谱里是显式的边。另外它做了框架感知的路由解析，还专门处理了 iOS 与 React Native / Expo 混合工程的桥接关系——这类跨语言边界通常是人工最难追的地方。

上手要几步？

三步。curl 或 npm 装 CLI，codegraph install 自动探测并接上你装了的 agent（Claude Code、Cursor、Codex CLI、opencode、Gemini CLI、Antigravity、Kiro、Copilot 都在列），然后在项目里 codegraph init 建图。之后 auto-sync 默认开着，文件一改索引就更新，不用自己重跑。不想用了有 codegraph uninstall 一次性回滚配置。

需要留意的地方：仓库里反复提到"托管版平台即将到来"和 beta 名额，说明现在这个 CLI 是更大商业产品的入口；默认带 telemetry，介意的人记得先看 Configuration 那节。

48 GB of VRAM on paper.
One GPU sitting completely idle.

The natural impulse when local models outgrow a single card is to buy a second one and treat the total pool like one giant bucket of memory. A builder testing this on a Threadripper 7960X paired an RTX 5090 with an RTX 5070 Ti to jump from 32 GB to 48 GB, expecting dual-Blackwell hardware to handle heavier weights cleanly. It even took replacing a four-slot 5070 Ti with a two-slot card just to clear the motherboard layout.

Then the actual benchmark arrived.

Splitting Qwen 3.8 27B at Q8 across both cards in llama.cpp cratered generation speed. The extra precision simply did not make up for the cross-card latency penalty. Falling back to Qwen 27B at Q4 loaded entirely onto the 5090 delivered a far faster, smoother experience, leaving the 5070 Ti doing nothing.

Splitting layers across asymmetric GPUs over standard PCIe turns the slower card and the bus into an active drag on your fastest silicon. If you have mismatched cards, do not force them into a single model pipeline. The practical move is isolating separate services: keep the primary LLM locked to the 5090, and hand image generation, video models, or a separate smaller session to the 5070 Ti.

Installed memory is just hardware inventory. Usable throughput depends on where the boundaries sit.

Seagate 和 Western Digital 過去幾年過得很爽。供給收緊，價格穩漲，毛利率 50% 以上，長約一路簽到 2028 甚至 2029，一切看起來都十分美好。
​
然後東芝拿著 3.8 億美元走進來說：「我想改一下劇本。」
​
東芝打算把這筆錢砸在菲律賓工廠，將 AI 資料中心用的硬碟產能翻倍，中期目標是把市占率從 10% 拉到 30%。
​
消息一出，Seagate 和 Western Digital 的股價馬上往下掉。
​
很多人會覺得奇怪，這兩家的長約明明鎖到 2028 年了，明年的獲利也不會怎樣因為這個消息而下跌，市場在怕什麼？
​
問題是，明年能賺多少，已經不是市場最在意的事情了。
​
大家真正在意的，是這個寡占市場的定價權還能撐多久。
​
▋老三為什麼一定要掀桌？
​
目前全球硬碟市場就三家在玩。Western Digital 占近 50%，Seagate 占 40% 出頭，東芝只有 10% 左右。
​
前兩名的最佳策略很簡單，大家維持紀律，不隨便擴產，讓價格穩定往上走。
​
過去幾年他們就是這麼做的，近線硬碟供給吃緊，價格穩穩漲，毛利率輕鬆爬上 50%，日子過得非常舒服。
​
但老三的算盤完全相反。東芝市占率才 10%，這是它大約五年來第一次對硬碟做大幅資本投入。資料中心需求突然爆發，自己產能卻卡在原點，現在每多賣一顆硬碟都是純增量收入。
​
它根本沒理由配合老大老二玩控制供給的遊戲。對它來說，最划算的打法就是擴產、給折扣、搶份額。
​
在寡占市場裡，龍頭通常不會自己砸盤，真正該擔心的永遠是急著突圍的落後者。
​
▋長約是氣囊，不是城牆
​
Seagate 2027 年前的產能已經透過長約分配完畢，價格也鎖定了。Western Digital 主要客戶的合約甚至拉到 2028 和 2029 年。所以明年財報絕對不會出事，毛利率撐得住，每股盈餘也會繼續成長。
​
但股價反映的是未來所有現金流的折現。長約保護的是已經簽好的出貨量，保護不了下次談判時的價格基準。
​
想像一下之後續約的場景。雲端客戶坐下來，手裡多了一張牌，他們可以很自然地跟龍頭業者說，東芝明年產能增加不少，希望你們主動給幾個百分點的折讓。
​
這張牌現在還沒出現，但市場已經在提前定價了。
​
▋技術領先能買多少時間？
​
雲端客戶挑硬碟，最終比的還是每 TB 價格、交期和供應穩定度。
​
不過在那之前，產品得先通過驗證，包含規格、韌體相容性、功耗以及能不能塞進現有機櫃。這道門檻確實存在，也幫技術領先者爭取到緩衝時間。
​
Seagate 的 HAMR 技術目前領先。40TB 產品已經在兩家超大雲端客戶出貨，44TB 正在驗證，50TB 目標設在 2027 年底。反觀東芝，65TB 量產要等到 2030 年。
​
這個時間差是真的，可能有一兩年甚至更久。
​
但在硬碟這種成熟產業，技術領先買到的時間往往比你想的短。一旦東芝儲存密度追上來、驗證通過，產品差異就會縮小成價格差異。
​
在比拼價格的市場裡，10% 市占的傢伙永遠比 40% 的更敢殺價。
​
▋三個值得盯的訊號
​
NAND 價格。 企業級固態硬碟每 TB 價格大約是硬碟的 20 倍，溫數據才被趕回機械硬碟。如果 2027 年下半年 NAND 供需轉平衡、固態硬碟價格開始鬆動，硬碟增量需求會先少一層，而東芝新產能剛好在那時候放量。
​
續約行為。 2028 年如果 Seagate 和 Western Digital 開始主動讓價，或是接受更短的合約期限，就代表買方籌碼已經變大了。
​
東芝產能流向。 新產能被超大雲端客戶的新增需求消化，價格不至於崩。但如果東芝硬碟開始出現在二線雲端和通路報價單上，就代表它在切老大老二的邊際市場了。
​
▋ 這週還有更多想聊的
​
究竟HDD的演化，會否令NAND和DRAM都出現同樣的情況？我們可以把他們再拆開來看。
​

​

主題四 | 東芝大舉擴產，存儲供不應求準備翻轉了？這篇的延伸版，我把 NAND、DRAM、HBM 的結構差異也一起拆了。

Upstream runtime flags will not save a 24 GB laptop when a 27B model hits physical memory limits.

Mainline llama.cpp PRs can optimize multi-token prediction and tune batch flags all day, but software flags cannot manufacture unified memory out of thin air. When you run Qwen 3.8 27B on a 24 GB M4 Pro MacBook, 64k of 8-bit context fills the machine completely. The workaround here was not waiting for an upstream merge, but tethering an iPhone 17 Pro Max over a 10 Gb/s USB-C cable to build an impromptu edge cluster.

The pipeline split is clean: for every 256-token prefill chunk, the Mac computes layers 1 through 40 and streams activations over the wire. The phone picks up layers 41 through 64 on its A19 Pro GPU while the laptop queues the next batch. Across context depths, the measured prefill gains hold up:

• 8k context: 132 tok/s climbs to 177 tok/s (+35%)
• 16k context: 109 tok/s climbs to 157 tok/s (+44%)
• 32k context: 101 tok/s climbs to 130 tok/s (+29%)
• 48k context: 87 tok/s climbs to 113 tok/s (+30%)

A cold 27k-token agent prefill dropped from 245 seconds on stock llama.cpp to 168 seconds wired to the phone.

Past 64k context, the architecture pivots. The phone stops computing split layers and turns into a remote context host. It absorbs up to 5.7 GB of KV cache (196k to 229k capacity), freezing Mac memory use. For old-context attention, 16k-key pages are compiled into Neural Engine models with the keys baked directly as weights. At 140k context, that shift dropped write latency from 279 ms down to 176 ms per token.

The friction is interface bandwidth. An iPhone caps out at 10 Gb/s USB 3.2, limits operation to single-request pipelines, and offers zero token generation speedup below 64k. But showing that heterogeneous mobile silicon can double as an auxiliary tensor engine sets an obvious target for testing faster 40 Gb/s Thunderbolt tablet links next.

I went to sleep. AI kept working.

This is one of the clearest examples I’ve had of what AI Native means in practice.

From midnight to around 7:45am, I gave AI several rounds of instructions and let it continue working within clear boundaries.

The job: use Colab L4 and A100 GPUs to generate 15-second 720p videos, compare speed, cost and quality, optimize the code, run repeated benchmarks, create videos, update a Pull Request, archive outputs to Google Drive, and shut down the GPUs when finished.

A few highlights:

00:10 — Set the task and limits: max 8 GPU hours, finish early if possible.

00:15–00:22 — Added requirements: optimize for both GPUs, minimum Q4 precision, organize the code into a PR.

01:41 — A separate 90-second English explainer video was delivered with Gemini voiceover, motion graphics and subtitles.

01:50 — First GPU tests completed, results saved, GPUs shut down, draft PR updated.

04:19 — I checked the results and corrected the methodology: one run wasn’t enough because model loading affects timing.

I asked for 5 consecutive generations per GPU, remove the slowest run, then calculate the average. AI also handled Colab connection problems and verified that every video was actually regenerated rather than cached.

07:39 — Final benchmark results

L4: 20m 25s/video
A100: 6m 18s/video
A100: about 3.24× faster
Estimated generation compute cost: only about 6% higher on A100

Across two rounds, 12 benchmark videos were generated.

Total GPU time, including setup and troubleshooting: about 3h 38m.

All GPUs were shut down automatically afterward.

Google Drive ended up with 16 videos + 16 matching thumbnails.

The draft PR was updated with the full benchmark results, and 119 tests passed.

The AI was not perfect. Some first-round videos still contained people and text even though the prompts explicitly prohibited them. Those failures were documented too.

For me, this is the important part:

AI Native does not mean “AI does everything correctly.”

It means:

I define the goal, boundaries, judgment and acceptance criteria. AI keeps executing within those boundaries.

I still review, correct and redirect when needed.

But I no longer need to sit in front of the computer doing every step myself.

Once the work is clearly defined, it can keep moving forward — even while I’m sleeping.

He says governments should help companies coordinate lawfully without violating antitrust or collusion rules.

He also argues that a permanent stop could be counterproductive. If responsible actors retreat while less cautious actors continue, the result may be more dangerous rather than safer. Pacing is meant to preserve development while creating time for evaluation, coordination and lawful rules.

制作流程：

我要使用抽帧，替换元素的方式，做一段视频，男子后面的半透明灵魂的造型 变成 各种多元宇宙的身份，比如 现代社会的老师，古代的皇帝，原始社会的野人等，每三帧更换一张。你先梳理一下，然后取一帧做一张图 我看下

4.确定 替换的角色，再下达完整指令，让GPT完整每帧图片的生成

可以先让AI提想法，然后你再增加和修改

5.检查图片细节，并基于细节错误 让AI重新修改

有个问题，很多张角色 的发型上面的这个 要去掉，戴帽子那些的不用处理。你看下哪几张有这个问题

6.下达 剪辑拼接的指令
GPT就会自己把这些图片 按照对应的时间线 进行 合成 并导出一个 完整的视频

这步剪辑 的工作量 比较大，就让GPT直接做了

7.人工拼接
这步因为太简单了，就不需要GPT做了、把GPT导出的视频和之前整段 的灵魂出窍掌 视频 拖到轨道上，进行拼接剪辑就完成了

Seedance 每日免费 额度 ，免费

就在几个月前，半导体还是人们热议的话题。

$NVDA、 $AMD、 $TSM、 $MU、 $ASML……随着 AI 爆发式发展，这个行业成为市场上的主要话题之一。

此后，随着7月份巨额的去杠杆 热度有所降温。但从数据来看，行业的情况远非如此。

市场继续以惊人的速度增长

7月，全球半导体销售额达到1468亿美元，同比增长135.1%，较6月增长6.4%。

这也是销售额连续第17个月环比增长。仅过了七个月，2026年的累计销售额就已超过该行业此前的年度纪录。

在股市上，行业表现仍然极为强劲
美国半导体基准指数 SOX 收于 13,136.67 点。

今年以来上涨 73.53%。

因此，尽管期间经历了数次调整，市场也对 AI 估值存在着诸多疑问，但整体趋势仍然非常强劲。

更重要的是，行业的发展已不再只围绕 GPU

AI 投资如今正在整条产业链上创造需求：HBM 内存、DRAM、先进封装、生产设备、网络与互连。

例如，Sk海力士 估计，到 2027 年，HBM 可能占全球 DRAM 产能的近 30%，而目前约为 20%。

因此，这已不再只是 $NVDA 的故事。算力需求越大，GPU 周边企业的战略重要性也越高。

下一阶段的要求可能会高得

需求确实存在，投资规模庞大，产能需求也在持续增长。

但在股价和支出如此大幅增长之后，市场接下来会期待其他东西：AI 带来的收入，能否真正从长期来看证明基础设施投资的合理性。

行业的下一阶段很可能将取决于这一点。

人们谈论半导体的频率也许不如几个月前，但目前的数据清楚表明，这一周期远未结束。

AI所带来的超级半导体周期 甚至刚刚加速发展

从open AI 的gpt迭代中就可以看到

原先迭代需要一年  现在迭代只需要一两个月 

我们正在处于这样一场伟大的历史变革当中！

AI正在范式转移我们所认知的一切

这是我一个乐观者的看法

让我以这样一句话结尾

悲观者是永远正确（因为这个世界上除了貔貅，没有只跌不涨的）

乐观者赢得一切！

存储被砸，光通信却越走越强：今天盘面真正变了
今天盘中到盘后，存储和光通信走出了非常鲜明的分化。表面看，都是AI数据中心产业链的一部分，但今天资金给出的答案完全不同：传统存储方向明显承压，光通信却继续获得关注。真正值得复盘的，不是简单看谁红谁绿，而是背后的逻辑正在重新排序。
先看存储。
今天WDC、STX这类传统硬盘方向压力非常明显。核心触发点来自东芝计划扩大HDD产能，目标到2027财年把相关产能较2025财年提高约一倍。市场第一反应非常直接：如果新增供给兑现，原本偏紧的供需格局可能被打破，因此WDC、STX盘中出现快速调整。MarketWatch披露，两家公司盘中一度均出现两位数幅度回落。
但这里有一个特别重要的细节：今天并不是整个存储方向一起走弱，而是传统HDD受冲击更明显。
从盘中结构看，DRAM相关指数甚至一度维持正向表现，说明市场并没有否定“AI带来的数据存储需求”这条逻辑，而是在重新区分不同产品的供需结构。
也就是说，今天真正发生的是存储内部的重新定价。
HDD面对的是未来新增产能和竞争格局变化；而HBM、DRAM、企业级SSD依然更多受到AI服务器需求和高端产品结构升级影响。因此后面看存储，不能再简单把WDC、MU、SNDK放在同一个逻辑里判断，而要拆开来看。
MU这边反而提供了另一个观察角度。最新一季数据和下一季度指引依然非常强，AI数据中心需求继续支撑DRAM和NAND业务，但市场已经开始从“数据好不好”转向“这么高的水平还能维持多久”。
这意味着存储现在已经进入一个更严格的阶段：不是有需求就行，而是需要不断证明高景气具有持续性。
再看光通信。
今天光通信的表现明显更强。AAOI盘中一度走高约8%，LITE和COHR也同步保持较强表现，说明资金不是只围绕单一标的，而是在整个高速互联方向形成联动。
这里的核心逻辑非常清楚。
AI集群规模越大，GPU之间需要交换的数据越多，对高速光连接的要求就越高。市场现在已经不满足于只讨论800G，而是在继续向1.6T、CPO、OCS延伸。
尤其OCS方向最近受到明显关注。Citi预计这一市场到2030年可能扩大到约110亿美元，并认为Google、Nvidia等大型客户可能进一步推动相关需求，而LITE和COHR被视为主要受益供应商之一。
今天盘面真正传递出来的信息是：
存储正在从“整个板块一起看”转向“内部重新筛选”，而光通信则正在从单一光模块逻辑，向更完整的AI高速互联体系扩散。

我觉得今天最大的变化不是存储弱、光通信强，而是市场开始更严格地区分“供给扩张带来的压力”和“AI新增需求带来的机会”。
接下来真正值得持续跟踪的，是谁还能不断拿出新的订单、需求和产业验证。
